canonPolicy.rule: Transit-family identities and recovered Path behavior remain authoritative. These normalized equations explain and compare that behavior. Numerical coefficients and thresholds are never canon unless separately adopted. Runtime speed/range authority remains in the existing live Path sources.

chi_g.meaning: normalized external gravity/curvature severity at the drive solution

chi_t.meaning: normalized tidal/shear severity across the affected volume

u_r.meaning: normalized route/reference uncertainty after covariance propagation

eta_f.meaning: fraction of conditioned drive-state effort producing useful family-specific transit effect

mu_s.meaning: structural support reserve against family-specific field, recoil, pressure, strain or topology load

b_c.meaning: normalized control bandwidth relative to fastest relevant field/environment disturbance

epsilon.meaning: usable energy/working-state reserve after required recovery reserve is protected

i_a.meaning: normalized infrastructure assistance from beacons, corridors, paired anchors or gateworks

p_fork.meaning: normalized probability/likelihood indicator of a route, topology, phase or state branch becoming ambiguous or destructive

h_abort.meaning: actionable warning time or solution distance remaining before the family-specific no-abort boundary

families.physicalAction: deform the local spacetime metric around a protected moving volume
families.distanceModel: effective metric geodesic; useful gain comes from reducing integrated route length in the engineered metric rather than increasing local hull velocity
families.gravityCoupling: external curvature consumes solution freedom and field authority; high gradients raise wall stress, horizon risk and energy burden
families.forkRisk: competing admissible tensor solutions or rapidly changing external curvature can force an unsafe sector solution
families.structuralLimit: field-wall gradients, emitter-sector support, hull deformation and coverage closure bound admissible compression
families.abortHorizon: last state from which envelope compression can be reduced and normal causal control/recovery retained before horizon or recovery authority is lost

families.forkRisk: two or more admissible planes can diverge faster than the controller can identify and commit to one
families.structuralLimit: plane-coupling force and differential gradient across the hull bound safe adherence
families.abortHorizon: look-ahead distance/time required to leave the plane before an unavoidable ridge, fork or gradient overload

families.physicalAction: create temporary topological adjacency between separated origin and destination volumes
families.distanceModel: reduce endpoint separation in the manipulated topology; transit distance becomes the engineered adjacency crossing rather than the original separation
families.gravityCoupling: external curvature changes the boundary conditions and energy/precision needed to make two volumes safely adjacent
families.forkRisk: multiple nearly valid endpoint topologies can map the fold boundary toward different destination volumes; destination occupancy is catastrophic
families.structuralLimit: aperture-ring load, topology waveguide stress, recoil/ringing support and complete closed-volume coverage
families.abortHorizon: the commit boundary at which adjacency formation is self-propagating or destination topology is locked; after this, recovery replaces steering
